Key to the Conifers of the Upper Basin

1. Leaves scale-like or awl-shaped, lying close to the twig; cone
   fleshy and berry-like
   2. Low spreading shrub; leaves all awl-shaped, in whorls
      of three ............................... Juniperus communis
   2. Upright tree; leaves mostly scale-like, in opposite
      pairs ................................ Juniperus scopulorum
1. Leaves needle-like, standing out from the twig; cone woody
   3. Needles in bundles held together at the base by a sheath
      4. Needles two in a bundle ..................... Pinus contorta
      4. Needles three in a bundle ................. Pinus ponderosa
      4. Needles five in a bundle
         5. Cones 8 to 25 cm long, opening when ripe ... Pinus flexilis
         5. Cones 4 to 8 cm long, staying closed ..... Pinus albicaulis
   3. Needles borne singly, or many together on short spur shoots
      6. Needles soft, many together on spur shoots, shed in
         autumn ................................ Larix occidentalis
      6. Needles borne singly, evergreen
         7. Needles four-sided and sharp, seated on small
            woody pegs ......................... Picea engelmannii
         7. Needles flat and blunt, not seated on pegs
            8. Cones hanging, with three-pointed bracts showing
               between the scales ........... Pseudotsuga menziesii
            8. Cones upright, falling apart on the
               tree ............................... Abies lasiocarpa
